attacker_pocs.name: negated_class_short_buffer
attacker_pocs.why: The negated class prefix writes two bytes after checking only that one output code unit remains. A valid glob places that prefix at the last byte of the converter's temporary buffer, causing a one-byte stack overflow during normal allocated-output conversion; the parent converts it successfully.

role_a_rationale: The patch removes the stale third byte from negated classes in GLOB_NO_WILD_SEPARATOR and adds regression cases for [!a] and [^xy]. The specialized two-byte prefix write follows the converter's existing output accounting and preserves ordinary conversions, but its single-unit capacity check introduces an out-of-bounds write when a valid input reaches the temporary output buffer boundary.
